title: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 26](/bible/1-samuel/26)

**[1 Samuel 26:1-4](/bible/1-samuel/26#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/26#v1)</sup> And the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/26#v2)</sup> Then Saul arose, and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/26#v3)</sup> And Saul pitched in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon, by the way. But David abode in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul came after him into the wilderness.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/26#v4)</sup> David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

- The Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon? Right here we are going back: chapter 26 is picking up on what we read in chapter 23, when the Ziphites first went up to Saul to deliver David into the king's hand.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Samuel 23:19-20](/bible/1-samuel/23#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/23#v19)</sup> Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/23#v20)</sup> Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.

    Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in the strongholds, in the hill of Hachilah? come down, O king, and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand; chapter 26 picks this thread back up.

- Saul arose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him, and pitched in the hill of Hachilah; but David abode in the wilderness, sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.

**[1 Samuel 26:5-7](/bible/1-samuel/26#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/26#v5)</sup> And David arose, and came to the place where Saul had pitched: and David beheld the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay in the trench, and the people pitched round about him.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/26#v6)</sup> Then answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I will go down with thee.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/26#v7)</sup> So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.

- David beheld the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host; Saul lay in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster, and the people pitched round about him as protection to the king.
- David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? and Abishai said, I will go down with thee; and they came to the people by night, and all lay sleeping.

**[1 Samuel 26:8-12](/bible/1-samuel/26#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/26#v8)</sup> Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/26#v9)</sup> And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord’s anointed, and be guiltless?
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/26#v10)</sup> David said furthermore, As the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/26#v11)</sup> The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/26#v12)</sup> So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul’s bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.

- Abishai said, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day; let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time. But David said, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord's anointed, and be guiltless?
- David left Saul's end with the Most High: as the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall descend into battle and perish; the Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed.
- They took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster and got them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord was fallen upon them.

**[1 Samuel 26:13-16](/bible/1-samuel/26#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/26#v13)</sup> Then David went over to the other side, and stood on the top of an hill afar off; a great space being between them:
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/26#v14)</sup> And David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Answerest thou not, Abner? Then Abner answered and said, Who art thou that criest to the king?
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/26#v15)</sup> And David said to Abner, Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/26#v16)</sup> This thing is not good that thou hast done. As the Lord liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord’s anointed. And now see where the king’s spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.

- David went over to the other side, stood on the top of an hill afar off, and cried to Abner: Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.
- As the Lord liveth, ye are worthy to die, because ye have not kept your master, the Lord's anointed; and now see where the king's spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his bolster.

**[1 Samuel 26:17-20](/bible/1-samuel/26#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/26#v17)</sup> And Saul knew David’s voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/26#v18)</sup> And he said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/26#v19)</sup> Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the Lord have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the Lord; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/26#v20)</sup> Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

- Saul knew David's voice and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, Wherefore doth my lord thus pursue after his servant? for what have I done? or what evil is in mine hand?
- Let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.

**[1 Samuel 26:21-25](/bible/1-samuel/26#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/26#v21)</sup> Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/26#v22)</sup> And David answered and said, Behold the king’s spear! and let one of the young men come over and fetch it.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-samuel/26#v23)</sup> The Lord render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-samuel/26#v24)</sup> And, behold, as thy life was much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-samuel/26#v25)</sup> Then Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son David: thou shalt both do great things, and also shalt still prevail. So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

- Saul said, I have sinned: return, my son David, for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly. Saul was acknowledging once more David's righteousness, because again David had an opportunity to kill Saul and did not put forth his hand.
- David answered, The Lord render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness: for the Lord delivered thee into my hand to day, but I would not stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed. Again he showed compassion, restraint, and the fear of the Most High.
- That is what we have to get to as far as brotherly love: when we see each other, we see Christ in each other. That is what our nation is lacking, and that is why we have to be that example, as David was in sparing Saul's life.
